I can’t diagnose you or tell you which tablets to buy — and with a **new persistent headache for 3 weeks plus vomiting on some mornings**, you should be assessed **urgently, ideally today**, rather than waiting for a GP appointment next week.

### What to do now in Manchester/NHS
- **Call NHS 111** and say:  
  “I’ve had a new headache most days for three weeks, and on some mornings I’ve been sick. I need advice urgently.”  
  They can triage you and arrange **same-day urgent care** if needed.
- Also **phone your GP practice first thing tomorrow** (or now if open) and ask to be seen urgently as a **new/worsening headache with vomiting** — many practices have out-of-hours urgent triage.
- If you can’t get seen and you feel worse, go to an **urgent treatment centre / minor injuries / A&E** depending on 111’s advice.

### Go to A&E or call 999 immediately if any of these are present
- Sudden severe “worst headache of my life” / “thunderclap” headache
- Confusion, difficulty waking, fainting, seizure
- Fever + stiff neck, or a new rash
- New weakness/numbness, slurred speech, vision loss/double vision, trouble walking/balance
- Headache after a head injury
- You are pregnant or recently postpartum
- You have a known cancer or are severely immunosuppressed
- Headache rapidly worsening or becoming much worse when lying down/straining

### While you’re waiting to be seen
- Rest in a quiet, dim room.
- Sip fluids to avoid dehydration.
- Avoid alcohol and screen time if it worsens.
- **Don’t drive** if you feel unwell, dizzy, or could be sick.

I know it’s frustrating to be stuck without an appointment, but this pattern deserves urgent professional assessment rather than self-treating with tablets bought today.
